verses.commentary: From inside the fish Jonah prayed. The belly of the beast becomes a prayer closet. What Jonah refused to do on the ship he now does in Sheol. Desperation accomplishes what duty could not.

In my distress I called. Jonah's psalm echoes dozens of other psalms. He prays with Scripture. From the realm of the dead (Sheol). The fish's belly becomes a metaphor for death itself. Yet even there, God hears.
You hurled me. Jonah acknowledges God's hand behind the sailors' hands. The waves and breakers are yours. No complaint about injustice. He recognizes divine justice in his drowning.
Banished from your sight. The presence he fled he now mourns losing. Yet I will look again toward your holy temple. Faith stirs in the depths. He looks toward what he ran from.
Seaweed wrapped around my head. Vivid detail. He was conscious, sinking, tangled. The deep surrounded him. Not poetic exaggeration but lived experience remembered in the fish.

To the roots of the mountains. The ancient cosmology: mountains anchored in the deep. He sank to the foundation of the world. The earth barred him in forever. Death seemed final. But you brought my life up from the pit. Rescue at the last moment.
When my life was ebbing away. At the point of death, he remembered the Lord. Memory of God saved him. Prayer rose to the temple. Even from the abyss, prayer reaches heaven.

Those who cling to worthless idols forfeit grace. Jonah critiques idol worship while still resisting God's mission to idol worshipers. Theological clarity does not guarantee obedient living. He sees others' failures more clearly than his own.

I will sacrifice with grateful praise. Thanksgiving before deliverance is complete. What I have vowed I will make good. Commitment renewed. Salvation comes from the Lord. The theological summary. Not from running, not from death, not from our plans. From the Lord alone.

The Lord commanded the fish. Creation obeys. The fish vomited Jonah onto dry land. Undignified delivery. The prophet emerges covered in fish vomit, gasping on the shore. Resurrection is not always pretty, but it is always God's work.
